_notes: Keycloak OIDC (realm masar, client masar-dashboard, Authorization Code + PKCE). The direct
password grant is disabled, so the real form has to be driven.
Step 2 settles the race between 'the login form appeared' and 'we were already signed in
via the SSO cookie'. `goto` resolves on domcontentloaded, before Keycloak renders, so
without it every onlyIfVisible step below sees nothing, skips, and the flow finishes still
sitting on the auth page having done nothing. The selector lists both outcomes and the
runner takes the first match.
THE LAST TWO STEPS SWITCH THE UI TO ENGLISH, AND THEY MATTER.
The dashboard is bilingual and DEFAULTS TO ARABIC (dir=rtl, lang=ar). The choice is kept in
localStorage under `lang`, which Playwright's storageState captures - so switching here, once,
in the cached login state, means every spec that reuses that state starts in English. Verified:
a fresh context built from the saved state opens /shipments with dir=ltr and lang=en.
Doing it per-spec instead would be both slower and unreliable, since a spec that forgot would
silently look for English text on an Arabic page and fail somewhere unrelated to its subject.
Every step is onlyIfVisible so the flow is idempotent: run against an already-authenticated
session, or one already in English, and it becomes a no-op rather than an error.
The final waitForVisible is the assertion. Once English is active the toggle reads AR, so
seeing an AR button is proof the switch actually happened rather than a hope that it did.
The two steps before the language switch dismiss a PRODUCTION-ACCESS DISCLAIMER modal
("Authorized Access Only...") that appears on login. It is a real modal backdrop, so it
intercepts every click underneath — including the EN toggle. Left in place it does not fail
with 'modal is open'; it fails with a click timeout on whatever the test tried to press next,
which is a much harder thing to diagnose. Tick the acknowledgement, then Accept.
